questions.q: For minimizing f(x) subject to g(x) = 0, how is the Lagrangian defined?
options: L(x,λ) = f(x) − g(x)
L(x,λ) = f(x) + λᵀg(x)
L(x,λ) = λf(x) + g(x)
L(x,λ) = f(x) · g(x)
questions.explain: The Lagrangian adds the objective to the multiplier-weighted constraint: L(x,λ) = f(x) + λᵀg(x). Its stationary points characterize the constrained optimum.

questions.q: In the minimum-variance portfolio problem with a budget and return constraint, what does setting ∇_w L = 0 give?
options: w = Σ1
Σw = λ1 + γμ, i.e. w = Σ⁻¹(λ1 + γμ)
w = μ − λΣ
w is independent of Σ
questions.explain: Differentiating L(w,λ,γ) = ½wᵀΣw − λ(1ᵀw−1) − γ(μᵀw−r_target) with respect to w gives Σw − λ1 − γμ = 0, so w = Σ⁻¹(λ1 + γμ).

questions.q: What does complementary slackness require in the KKT conditions?
options: All multipliers must equal zero
Every constraint must be an equality
For each inequality constraint, the product of its multiplier and the constraint value must be zero
The Hessian must be negative definite
questions.explain: Complementary slackness means a multiplier can only be nonzero if its inequality constraint is exactly binding (tight); a slack (non-binding) constraint must have a zero multiplier.

questions.q: Economically, what does a Lagrange multiplier represent at the optimum?
options: The variance of the portfolio
A random noise term with no interpretation
The shadow price — how much the optimal objective value changes per unit relaxation of that constraint
The number of assets in the portfolio
questions.explain: Lagrange multipliers measure the marginal sensitivity of the optimal objective value to a small change in the corresponding constraint, which is why they're called shadow prices.

questions.q: Why does scipy.optimize.minimize with method='SLSQP' and equality constraints reproduce the same weights as the closed-form Lagrangian solution?
options: SLSQP ignores the constraints and just minimizes the unconstrained objective
SLSQP numerically solves the same first-order KKT stationarity system that the Lagrangian derivation solves algebraically
SLSQP always returns the equal-weight portfolio
It is a coincidence specific to this dataset
questions.explain: SLSQP (Sequential Least Squares Programming) is a numerical method for exactly the KKT conditions derived from the Lagrangian, so it converges to the same stationary point as the algebraic solution.
